text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Roman Catholic Bishop Ndingi Mwana a'Nzeki says he has received death threats because of his persistent criticism of the government.
- Opposition parties protest against confessions by two men at a presidential rally that they were recruited and trained as guerrillas by the opposition.
- A nominated member of parliament accuses opposition party leader Kenneth Matiba of misleading Kenyans.
- An opposition alliance has vowed to hold a national convention to change the constitution.
- Twelve school pupils are stranded in the bush near Nairobi National Park after being duped they were being admitted to an ultra-modern school in Nairobi.
- Opposition Democratic Party of Kenya chairman Mwai Kibaki dismisses claims by two self-confessed guerrillas as a ruling party ploy to create panic and fear among Kenyans.
- The Belgian ambassador to Tanzania says the Belgian government will not compensate relatives of some 700 people who drowned when the Belgian-built ferry Bukoba capsized on May 21.
- Uganda's secretary of treasury says high officials have diverted budgeted funds to buy vehicles for ministers.
- The National Hospital Insurance Fund of Kenya may lose 274 million shillings following the collapse of the Heritage Bank.
